caption: Figure 3: Overview of HorizonStream. Given an RGB stream, the model causally processes the most recent WW frames. Gated Window Attention handles local matching, Geometric Linear Attention propagates long-range geometry with an O⁡(1)O(1) recurrent geometric state, and Metric Readout Tokens recover stable scale and pose. An optional loop-closure module refines the trajectory.

In training, the point loss ℒpt\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{pt}} compares 𝑿\bm{X} with the ground truth 𝑿gt\bm{X}^{\mathrm{gt}}, and the solid angle d​Ω\mathrm{d}\Omega of the same 𝑹\bm{R} weighs the error of each pixel, shown here on the panorama, where cells of equal pixel count cover unequal areas of the sphere.

caption: Figure 4: Overview of GPA-VGGT. Early blocks 00–88 replace global attention with frame attention augmented by a shared cross-frame K/V set containing special tokens and content-adaptive pooled image-token summaries. Later blocks 99–2323 preserve all queries and merge only K/V tokens, using a weaker merge ratio in the core blocks 1313–1616. (a) Pooled summaries are constructed by assigning patch tokens to stride-8 seeds according to cosine similarity and averaging the K/V tokens within each content-adaptive cluster; the summary size determines the +log⁡s+\log s correction. (b) K/V matching is computed after a 128128-dimensional Gaussian projection, while all queries are retained for global attention.
